source: Yale Bright Star Catalogue, 5th revised edition (Hoffleit and Warren 1991), CDS catalogue V/50, file 'catalog' (byte-identical to http://tdc-www.harvard.edu/catalogs/bsc5.dat.gz). Proper names: IAU Catalog of Star Names (IAU-CSN), IAU Working Group on Star Names, https://www.pas.rochester.edu/~emamajek/WGSN/IAU-CSN.txt (last updated 2022-04-04). Planets and the Moon: NASA JPL Horizons, see planets_method.

time.local_text: Friday 9 October 2026, 22:00 WEST (UTC+1; Portugal returns to WET on 25 October 2026)

method: Stars with visual magnitude 4.5 or brighter. J2000 catalogue positions precessed to the date with the IAU 1976 precession angles (Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 21); proper motion, nutation and aberration ignored (each under 1 arcminute here). Greenwich mean sidereal time from Meeus (12.4), UT1 taken as UTC. Altitude is geometric, with no atmospheric refraction. Azimuth in degrees from north through east (0 = N, 90 = E, 180 = S, 270 = W). Only stars above the horizon (alt > 0) are kept. ra and dec are the catalogue's J2000 values in degrees; bv is the catalogue's B-V colour index (null when absent). name is the IAU WGSN proper name when the star has one, else null; bsc_designation is the catalogue's Bayer/Flamsteed label as written in BSC5.
planets_method: Planets and the Moon from NASA JPL Horizons (https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/horizons/), observer at the same place and time, airless apparent azimuth and elevation (no refraction, like the stars), Horizons' apparent visual magnitude, queried 2026-10-04. planets lists the bodies above the horizon and at magnitude 4.5 or brighter, the same cut as the stars: only Saturn, five days after its opposition, low in the east-south-east and brighter than every star in this list except Vega and Capella. checked_below_cut lists every other planet and the Moon, so that none is drawn by mistake: the Moon (new, under 1 percent lit), Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter are below the horizon; Uranus and Neptune are above it but fainter than 4.5.
